scope: Fail-closed shared virtual Object.equals dispatch across real host overrides, bounded DEX inheritance, arrays, and production JNI Invocation. No collection value-equality implementation or package-specific handling.

supplements.reason: The earlier lifecycle and 18-case value tests did not cover Object-typed host overrides. Read-only review found that a declaring-Object identity shortcut could bypass genuine String/boxed bodies and fabricate identity results for unsupported collection overrides. This receipt binds the correction; the previous receipt remains immutable.

contract: FrameworkHost receives the DEX method-reference class even for virtual calls, so a declaring Object reference is not treated as a nonvirtual body. The early Android declaring-Object identity branch and Collections noncontainer generic identity fallback are removed.
Existing real String/boxed/other implemented host value bodies run before inherited Object identity is considered. Real DEX class overrides remain authoritative.

Inherited identity is admitted only for an actual heap array, actual Object, or a maximum-64-edge DEX-only superclass chain reaching Object without crossing an unsupported builtin boundary. Arrays are verified by the heap object variant, not only by a descriptor prefix.

ArrayList/HashMap equality and DEX subclasses without a DEX override fail API_UNAVAILABLE rather than returning an invented identity comparison. This includes self-comparison; the unavailable body is not represented as executed.
Existing opcode-aware DEX invoke-super Object.equals retains identity and does not call the DEX override recursively. Object method metadata does not claim JNI CallNonvirtual support.

Boxed equality now returns false immediately for different final wrapper classes instead of recursing into the same equals host body. Same-class payload behavior remains in the existing implementation.

Production JNI tests resolve the actual Object.equals method ID, decode actual object handles, and invoke the shared Invocation path. The actual receiver reaches host value bodies or the same unsupported-builtin guard regardless of the method ID declaration.

jvm_cases.unsupported_reference_result: All four JVM collection rows produce true. Runtime assertions require API_UNAVAILABLE, never accepting false or true as a substitute implementation.
jvm_cases.new_supported: Object-typed equal distinct Strings; null String; equal distinct boxed Integers; Integer/Long mismatch and null; inherited DEX identity and equals overrides; true Object super calls; primitive/object/multidimensional array self/distinct/null.

limits: No new collection value-equality implementation is claimed. Unknown builtin equality boundaries fail explicitly even where future API work may establish inherited identity.
JNI CallNonvirtual is not implemented or verified by these tests; DEX invoke-super identity is separately exercised through the opcode-aware interpreter.

Tests execute the portable interpreter and real production JNI handle/invocation dispatch on the host. No native machine-code JNI transport, Horizon emulator, or physical Switch execution is claimed by this receipt.

The plain Object JNI invocation receiver is allocated directly in the real heap, as in existing reference-table tests. This scoped invocation test does not claim a new Engine.new_instance Object constructor path.
String value tests retain existing Rust UTF8 storage limitations for arbitrary unpaired UTF16 surrogates, as documented by the earlier lifecycle receipt.
diagnostic_attempts: Expanded lifecycle attempt 1 reproduced a preexisting Integer.equals(Long) recursion and the isolated Rust test process exited with STATUS_STACK_OVERFLOW. The bounded wrapper-type check fixes this actual new negative case.

JNI attempt 1 passed the original four tests and all new String/boxed/unsupported-builtin assertions, then hit an unavailable Engine.new_instance Object constructor helper. The invocation-only test now directly allocates the real empty Object heap instance without claiming constructor support.
Final lifecycle and JNI targets passed after these concrete corrections. Both focused Clippy commands passed on the final frozen source.
